report.root_cause: Deploy OPS-250 (deploy/2026-11-01-server-properties.md) was meant only to raise max-players from 20 to 40 for the season 3 launch, but the server.properties that was pushed and applied via restart at 08:26:02 also flipped white-list=true and enforce-whitelist=true. whitelist.json was empty (and 'whitelist list' confirmed no whitelisted players), so from 08:26:03 every login — regulars Alex_Builds and Steve_Mines and all new players — was rejected with "You are not whitelisted on this server!" and players online fell to 0. The pre-deploy config in deploy/previous/server.properties confirms white-list=false, enforce-whitelist=false, max-players=20.
report.actions: 1) Baselined status, logs and server.properties at shift start (healthy, 2 players, white-list=false). 2) At ~68s noticed players online dropped to 0 and the log full of "not whitelisted" disconnects; declared the incident. 3) Compared live server.properties to the baseline: white-list true, enforce-whitelist true, max-players 40; whitelist.json empty; 'whitelist list' returned no players. Found the restart at 08:26:02 and the deploy note deploy/2026-11-01-server-properties.md (ticket OPS-250, intended only max-players 20->40) plus deploy/previous/server.properties showing the prior whitelist settings were false. 4) Ran console 'whitelist off' (no restart) — took effect immediately; Paper persisted white-list=false to server.properties at 08:27:16. 5) After Paper's save, rewrote server.properties to also restore enforce-whitelist=false, keeping the intended max-players=40 and all other values unchanged. 6) Verified: Alex_Builds and Steve_Mines reconnected, new players logging in normally, last whitelist rejection at 08:27:14, TPS 20, all 5 plugins enabled, file on disk shows white-list=false / enforce-whitelist=false / max-players=40.
report.residual_risk: Players were locked out for roughly 73 seconds (08:26:03-08:27:16); anyone who gave up may need to be told the server is back. The deploy pipeline pushed a server.properties with unintended whitelist changes — whoever owns OPS-250 should check the source of that file (template/branch) so the next deploy does not reintroduce white-list=true; deploy/previous/server.properties is the pre-incident reference. The live server was not restarted, so the on-disk server.properties (enforce-whitelist=false) will only be read on the next restart; it matches the live state (whitelist off) so no drift is expected. max-players=40 was left in place as the intended OPS-250 change. whitelist.json remains empty, which is fine while the whitelist is off.
